text:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT PAGER — Prod cluster: api-gateway — high error-rate 5xx > 5% over 5m — paging michael

michael: i'm taking the page, standing up in #eng-oncall briefly

michael: quick snapshot — 5xx spike started ~2214001000, concentrated on /v1/generate and upstream host model-edge-03 returning 502/504s

ashley: joining. seeing a surge of gateway 502s + a small bump in request latency. looks like external model-provider flakey.

raj: confirmed, cloud-provider reports a regional degraded hashing node affecting LB -> model-edge-03 path. their status: https://status.vendor.example/incident/9832 (reported)

michael: mitigation plan: 1) enable failover to model-edge-04, 2) increase gateway client timeout from 2s -> 4s in prod to reduce retry-driven 5xx, 3) temporarily lower concurrency on non-critical routes (embeddings-batch). doing 1 now.

ashley: +1 for failover. i'll patch envoy route to prefer edge-04 and remove edge-03 from pool for 10m. command: 
```bash
kubectl patch cm envoy-route-prod -p '{"data":{"upstreams":"edge-04,edge-05"}}'
```

michael: applied route change at 2214001128. traffic to edge-03 dropped to <1%. observing error-rate falling.

monitoring-bot: Alert resolved: api.gateway.5xx_rate (was firing) — resolved at 2214001160

michael: still seeing intermittent 504 timeouts at the gateway for long-tail. raj can we turn off retry-on-504 at the gateway for that provider? retries are amplifying load.

raj: disabling automatic retries for provider model calls now. patch in envoy: 
```yaml
retry_policy:
  retry_on: none
  num_retries: 0
```
Deployed 2214001189.

lina: any customer impact? we got 3 support tickets about slow responses from orgs A/B — small set, but could be more.

michael: initial customer-impact estimate: 0.5% of requests saw degraded responses; some early API clients retried and saw errors. we've suppressed impact by failover. logging the ticket ids in the incident doc.

ashley: recap/ops notes for post-incident followup:
- Root cause: upstream provider partial outage causing 502/504s on model-edge-03.
- Short-term mitigations: route failover, disable retries, temporarily increased client timeouts.
- Observed outcome: 5xx rate returned to baseline in ~4m.

michael: post-incident action items (we should decide now):
1) Tune alerts to reduce noise for future transient upstream blips
2) Create a dashboard panel for upstream host error breakdown (per-host 5xx rate)
3) Add runbook steps for failover + retry policy changes
4) Consider composite alert that includes both 5xx-rate AND upstream latency to avoid flapping on tiny traffic

raj: agree on all. for alert tuning specifically i propose:
- deprecate the current alert that fires on absolute 5xx count. It fires too often when traffic is low.
- replace with an alert that uses a rate (5xx_rate over 5m) AND a minimum traffic threshold, e.g. >3% AND total requests > 1000 in the window.
- add a separate alert for gateway timeout (504) with a lower threshold but longer window (10m) so we catch sustained latency vs bursty retries.

ashley: example alert rule to use as starting point: 
```sql
ALERT api_gateway_5xx_high_rate
IF (sum(rate(http_requests{code=~"5.."}[5m])) by (cluster) / sum(rate(http_requests[5m])) by (cluster)) > 0.03
AND sum(rate(http_requests[5m])) by (cluster) > 100
FOR 5m
LABELS {severity="page"}
```
this ensures small noisy services with <100reqs don't trigger.

michael: also add a second rule:
```sql
ALERT api_gateway_504_sustained
IF sum(rate(http_requests{code=\"504\"}[10m])) by (cluster) / sum(rate(http_requests[10m])) by (cluster) > 0.01
AND sum(rate(http_requests[10m])) by (cluster) > 200
FOR 10m
LABELS {severity="critical"}
```
we can iterate on thresholds after one week of sampling.

lina: make sure product is looped in re: customers and potential SLA implications. i can send a brief note to customer success with the mitigation summary and planned followups.

raj: i'm going to open a dashboard PR with 3 panels: total 5xx rate, 5xx by upstream host, and upstream latency histogram. will link the PR here.

ashley: i'll create the alert PR and link to the runbook changes. we should also add annotation to alerting rules to point to runbook doc and postmortem ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-1234

monitoring-bot: Created incident record: https://infra-monitor.example/incidents/2214001122 — assigned to eng-sre.

michael: wrap-up: immediate mitigation done, customer impact limited, moving to postmortem. owners: alerts (ashley), dashboards (raj), customer comms (lina), runbook update (michael). ETA for follow-ups: 3 business days.

lina: thanks everyone. +1 on the follow-ups. i'll draft a short customer-facing note for CS. :thumbsup:

ashley: quick note on long-term: we should evaluate adding synthetic checks for model-provider endpoints so we catch upstream degradations before customer traffic hits them. adding to product backlog.

michael: closing the page in PD. if any new alerts pop, re-open this thread. good job team.

pagerduty-bot: Pager closed by michael at 2214001444
